gen.site.blogHint: Articles you want read and cited
gen.site.docsHint: Wants to be in AI answers
gen.goal.block-training: No AI training, stay in AI search
gen.goal.block-trainingHint: Blocks training crawlers and training tokens; AI search and user-requested fetches stay allowed.
gen.goal.block-all-aiHint: Blocks AI training, AI search and AI assistants. Google, Bing and Apple search stay allowed.
gen.goal.allow-allHint: No AI rules. Optionally state your preferences with Content-Signal.
gen.goal.customHint: Pick allow or block for each of the {count} documented AI agents.
gen.exceptionsHint: Open a path even to blocked AI bots, or close a path even to allowed ones.
gen.globalHint: Paths for User-agent: * — search engines included. One per line.
gen.signalsHint: Optional Content-Signal line (Cloudflare proposal; not a standard and ignored by Google).
gen.communityTitle: Also list {count} agents from the ai.robots.txt community list
gen.communityHint: Unverified names collected by the ai.robots.txt project. They follow the same goal.
gen.commentsTitle: Explain each section with # comments in the file
gen.verified: Verified: {agents} agents × {paths} paths match the policy
gen.notVerified: Verification failed for {count} checks — please report this file
gen.warnVisibility: Blocked here: {names}. These power AI search and assistant answers, so your pages will not be cited by them.
gen.warnNonCompliant: {names} may ignore robots.txt (operator statement or reports). Add server rules if you must keep them out.
gen.warnGroupRule: Bots named in their own group ignore the User-agent: * group — so the * rules are repeated in AI groups where needed.
gen.mergeHint: Paste the file. It stays in your browser.
gen.mergeKeep: Leave agents that already have their own group as they are
gen.mergeReplace: Replace their groups with the new policy
gen.mergeEquivalent: Unchanged for existing agents: {agents} user-agents × {paths} paths checked, no difference.
gen.mergeNotEquivalent: Warning: {count} decisions changed for existing agents.
gen.mergeEmpty: Paste your robots.txt to see the merged file.

note.header: Header comment: when and how the file was made.
note.policy: Comment stating the policy in plain words.
note.user-agent: Names a crawler. Consecutive User-agent lines share the rules below.
note.user-agent-token: A robots.txt-only token: no crawler sends it; it controls how content fetched by another crawler may be used.
note.disallow-all: Blocks every path for the agents above.
note.allow-exception: Re-opens this path for the agents above (longer rule wins).
note.block-exception: Closes this path for the agents above.
note.repeat-global: Repeated from User-agent: * because a named agent ignores the * group.
note.global-group: Rules for every crawler that has no group of its own (Google, Bing and others).
note.global-disallow: Closed to every crawler without its own group.
note.content-signal: Content-Signal: how content may be used after access (Cloudflare proposal).
note.sitemap: Location of your XML sitemap; applies to all crawlers.
note.separator: Closes the previous group without changing it.

tester.pasteHint: The text stays in your browser; nothing is uploaded.
tester.testNoRule: No rule matches this path, so it is allowed.
tester.testGroupSpecific: {agent} has its own group (lines {lines}); the * group does not apply to it.
tester.testGroupGlobal: {agent} has no group of its own, so it follows User-agent: * (lines {lines}).
tester.testGroupNone: There are no groups for {agent} or *, so everything is allowed.
tester.http.4xx: HTTP {status}: Google treats a 4xx answer (except 429) as “no robots.txt” — everything may be crawled.
tester.http.5xx: HTTP {status}: Google treats a 5xx or 429 answer as “crawling not allowed” for the moment and retries; after about 30 days it may use a cached copy or treat the site as unrestricted.
tester.contentType: Content-Type is {type}, not text/plain. Google still reads it; some crawlers may not.
tester.htmlBody: The response looks like an HTML page, not a robots.txt file. A soft 404? Crawlers will find no valid rules.
tester.truncated: Only the first 512 KiB were fetched. Google ignores everything after 500 KiB.
tester.crossHost: The request was redirected to another host ({host}). Google follows up to 5 redirects and applies the final file.
tester.err.invalid-url: That does not look like a website address.
tester.err.scheme-not-allowed: Only http:// and https:// addresses can be checked.
tester.err.port-not-allowed: Only the standard ports 80 and 443 can be checked.
tester.err.host-not-allowed: This hostname is internal or reserved and cannot be checked.
tester.err.ip-not-public: Private, local and reserved IP addresses cannot be checked.
tester.err.address-not-public: The hostname points to a private or reserved address, so it was not contacted.
tester.err.credentials-not-allowed: Addresses with a user name or password cannot be checked.
tester.err.dns-failed: The domain name could not be resolved.
tester.err.too-many-redirects: More than 5 redirects — Google stops following at this point too.
tester.err.redirect-invalid: A redirect pointed to an invalid address.
tester.err.timeout: The server did not answer within 5 seconds.
tester.err.connection-failed: Could not connect to the server.
tester.err.tls-failed: The HTTPS certificate could not be verified.
tester.err.rate-limited: Too many checks from your address. Try again in {seconds} s, or paste the file instead.
tester.err.network: Our checker could not be reached. You can still paste the file.
tester.err.internal-error: Something went wrong on our side.

lint.file-too-large: The file is {bytes} bytes. Google reads only the first 500 KiB and ignores the rest.
lint.bom: The file starts with a byte order mark (BOM). Google skips it; some parsers do not.
lint.invalid-line: Not a “key: value” line — ignored by crawlers.
lint.missing-colon: No colon after “{key}”. Google accepts it; other crawlers may not.
lint.typo-key: “{key}” is a misspelling Google tolerates; other crawlers ignore the line. Write “{expected}”.
lint.nonstandard-key: “{key}” is read as “{expected}” by Google only because it starts with it. Use the exact key.
lint.unknown-directive: “{key}” is not a standard directive; most crawlers ignore it.
lint.crawl-delay: Crawl-delay is ignored by Google; Bing and Yandex honour it.
lint.noindex-directive: “{key}” in robots.txt is not supported (Google dropped it in 2019). Use a robots meta tag or X-Robots-Tag.
lint.content-signal: Content-Signal (Cloudflare proposal) states how content may be used. Not a standard; Google says it has no effect.
lint.content-signal-invalid: Content-Signal values must be search, ai-input or ai-train set to yes or no.
lint.content-usage: Content-Usage comes from IETF aipref drafts (not an RFC yet); crawler support is not established.
lint.content-usage-invalid: Content-Usage expects an optional path and preferences like train-ai=n, search=y.
lint.cloudflare-managed: A block managed by Cloudflare. Cloudflare puts it before your own rules and updates it itself.
lint.rule-before-user-agent: This rule comes before any User-agent line, so no crawler applies it.
lint.empty-user-agent: Empty User-agent value. Use * or a crawler name.
lint.user-agent-version: Only “{token}” of “{value}” is used for matching. Write just the token.
lint.user-agent-nonstandard: “{value}” contains characters RFC 9309 does not allow in a product token (only letters, “-” and “_”). Google's parser reads it as “{token}”; the crawler's own parser may differ.
lint.user-agent-invalid: “{value}” does not start with a valid token, so it matches no crawler.
lint.unknown-agent: “{token}” is not a known crawler token. Did you mean “{suggestion}”?
lint.pattern-no-leading-slash: “{pattern}” does not start with / or *, so it never matches. Did you mean “/{pattern}”?
lint.pattern-full-url: Allow and Disallow take a path such as /private/, not a full URL. This rule never matches.
lint.dollar-in-middle: “$” means “end of URL” only as the last character.
lint.redundant-wildcard: A trailing “*” changes nothing: rules already match by prefix.
lint.group-without-rules: The group for {agents} has no rules: these crawlers may fetch everything and ignore the * group.
lint.blank-line-does-not-split: The blank line does not start a new group: “{agent}” shares the rules below with “{previous}”.
lint.specific-overrides-global: {agent} has its own group, so {count} rule(s) from User-agent: * no longer apply to it (e.g. {example}).
lint.duplicate-group: “{agent}” appears in {count} groups (lines {lines}). Google merges them; some crawlers use only the first.
lint.disallow-all-global: User-agent: * with Disallow: / blocks every crawler without its own group — Google and Bing included.
lint.sitemap-relative: Sitemap needs a full URL such as https://example.com/sitemap.xml.
lint.line-too-long: Line longer than about 16 KB — the rest is cut off.
lint.no-groups: No User-agent groups: the file allows everything.
lint.ai-search-blocked: Blocking {agents} removes the site from these AI search and assistant answers.
lint.token-only-agent: {token} is a control token, not a crawler: it does not affect regular search.
lint.non-compliant-bot: {agents}: may not follow robots.txt. Block them at the server or CDN too.
